options.counterfactual: Every finite AW*-factor is monotone sequentially complete: every bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound.
options.approach: Check the precise hypotheses and conclusion of the finite AW*-algebra completeness theorem in the available materials. If it establishes sequential completeness in the ordinary operator order, apply it directly to exclude every proposed witness.

options.counterfactual: Every finite AW*-factor is monotone sequentially complete: every bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound.
options.approach: Investigate whether bounded quasitrace-metric completeness, combined with a separate monotone Cauchy result, proves sequential completeness. Keep those two assertions distinct and verify each before applying them.

options.counterfactual: For every finite 2-quasitrace q, positive elements with uniformly bounded partial sums necessarily satisfy q(b_n) tending to zero, even without any order-completeness assumption on the algebra.
options.approach: Seek a dimension-free estimate bounding the number of increments whose quasitrace exceeds a fixed positive threshold. Such an estimate would immediately exclude the constant positive increments required in the problem.

options.counterfactual: For every finite 2-quasitrace q, positive elements with uniformly bounded partial sums necessarily satisfy q(b_n) tending to zero, even without any order-completeness assumption on the algebra.
options.approach: Use spectral cutoffs to turn the increments into projections with bounded partial sums and uniformly positive quasitrace. Try to exclude that projection family using matrix amplification and finite dimension theory.

options.counterfactual: For every finite 2-quasitrace q, positive elements with uniformly bounded partial sums necessarily satisfy q(b_n) tending to zero, even without any order-completeness assumption on the algebra.
options.approach: Investigate whether the restriction of a 2-quasitrace to a norm-summable positive series has an exhaustion property stronger than its usual continuity estimates. Establish precisely what additional argument extends that property to merely bounded positive partial sums.

options.counterfactual: A finite AW*-factor with a nonlinear faithful normalized 2-quasitrace can be converted into a witness for some positive eta in the problem.
options.approach: Start from a positive additivity defect and investigate whether matrix amplification and repeated decompositions turn it into arbitrarily long positive partitions with uniformly large quasitrace values. Identify the extra compactness needed to obtain one infinite sequence.

options.counterfactual: A finite AW*-factor with a nonlinear faithful normalized 2-quasitrace can be converted into a witness for some positive eta in the problem.
options.approach: Examine whether failure of linearity forces failure of monotone sequential completeness. If it does, use quasitrace-metric completeness and constant-gap interpolation to construct the required sequence while preserving its upper-bound set.
